IR.rationale: A rising 5-year yield relative to the policy rate signals a repricing of the expected rate path. It carries duration losses and tighter financing conditions into HY and EM dollar bonds over the following weeks.

B.rationale: Spread widening that comes with weak HY returns marks forced selling and liquidity-driven price pressure. Credit markets tend to partly reverse this as the risk premium is earned back.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility proxies elevated risk aversion and a high price of risk. That predicts higher subsequent compensation for holding credit.

AP.rationale: Strong equity weeks tend to be priced into credit quickly. The equity-credit lead is weak and partly reversing, so this state captures overextended risk-on pricing.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum payoffs reflect crowded trend-following in risk assets. These tend to precede weaker forward risk premia.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength tightens global dollar funding and EM borrowers' balance sheets. This weighs on EM sovereign and leveraged credit returns.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity gains support commodity-exporting sovereigns and energy/materials issuers that are heavily weighted in HY and EM indices.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions summarise funding stress and lower risk-bearing capacity of intermediaries. That shapes near-term credit returns.

ENDG.rationale: Credit index returns show short-horizon autocorrelation from stale pricing and slow-moving flows, so recent strength carries information about the next weeks.

IR.rationale: A rising 1-year rate over the funds rate signals hawkish repricing of near-term policy. Such shifts historically raise volatility in spread and EM dollar markets.

B.rationale: Joint losses in HY and EM bonds indicate a broad credit risk-off. By the leverage effect and volatility clustering, this precedes higher realised variance.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility across both equity and safe-haven assets signals broad, cross-asset uncertainty. Such uncertainty spills into credit volatility beyond its own history.

AP.rationale: Simultaneous weakness in US and EM equities signals a global risk-off. This predicts rising credit volatility through the equity-credit link of structural models.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects flight-to-quality within equities. It tends to accompany deteriorating credit conditions and higher volatility.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation is a classic global funding-stress signal, especially for EM sovereign debt. It precedes higher realised volatility.

COM.rationale: Commodity price declines hit EM exporters and HY energy issuers. This raises default-risk uncertainty and bond price volatility.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reduce dealer and investor risk capacity, which amplifies price moves in less liquid credit markets.

ENDG.rationale: High recent variance relative to its history tends to mean-revert faster than a simple persistence model implies. That makes it informative for the excess component.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening from rising long yields delivers duration losses and tighter long-term financing. This raises the chance of a sharp drawdown in long-duration EM and HY bonds.

B.rationale: Widening corporate spreads signal rising default and risk premia. Spread shocks cluster, raising the probability of further large losses.

V.rationale: Broad elevated implied volatility widens the return distribution and marks fragile risk appetite. Tail outcomes become more likely.

AP.rationale: Weak EM equities lead EM sovereign spreads and signal capital outflows from risky dollar debt.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry little documented information about credit tail losses.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar tightens EM financing and raises sovereign default risk, a key channel for large EM bond losses.

COM.rationale: Commodity slumps impair the fiscal positions of exporters and the solvency of energy HY issuers. This fattens the left tail.

MC.rationale: Joint tightness in financial conditions and elevated measured stress identifies systemic strain, under which credit drawdowns concentrate.

ENDG.rationale: Credit losses cluster through slow-moving outflows and stale pricing, so recent weak returns raise the odds of a further tail loss.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates generate duration gains and easier financing. This raises the chance of a strong rally.

B.rationale: After spread widening, the risk premium is high and relief rallies from spread compression are more likely and larger.

V.rationale: High volatility widens the distribution in both directions and coincides with high risk premia. Both make large rebounds more likely.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities signal improving EM risk appetite and inflows that carry over to EM and HY bonds.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum payoffs typically occur at turning points when beaten-down risky assets rebound. Such states coincide with sharp credit rallies.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global dollar funding conditions and EM balance-sheet pressure. That supports strong EM and HY bond rallies.

COM.rationale: Commodity strength improves the credit quality of EM exporters and HY energy issuers, raising the probability of outsized gains.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress raises both dispersion and expected compensation. Large gains tend to follow stress peaks.

ENDG.rationale: Large rebounds tend to follow weak recent returns, as liquidity-driven selling reverses.
